title: A closed duplicate PR is not proof that every bundled fix landed
applies_when: An existing PR bundles distinct changes and is closed as duplicate, superseded or partly replaced, while a candidate is being rejected as already fixed.
lesson: Follow the maintainer's replacement link, compare the exact affected function/hunk with current source, and run the real consumer if coverage remains uncertain. A duplicate label applies to the discussed overlap, not automatically to every bundled hunk. Preserve original authorship; an untreated hunk can justify supplemental evidence or a coordinated narrow follow-up, not claiming a new discovery or automatically opening a competing PR.
avoid_when: Do not revive a rejected behavior change merely because it is absent from main. An active author-owned replacement remains their work. Respect explicit maintainer decisions, security-reporting rules and repository contribution policy. Source comparison proves presence or absence of a guard, not production prevalence, exploitability, full CI or publication permission.

evidence.note: The bundled local-object and ciphertext-boundary proposal includes nonce-length validation and was closed with a duplicate #7425 comment. Closure alone does not say each change was merged.
The merged replacement's four-file scope is filestore key-path containment, not encrypted-object nonce handling.
Original author's unmerged hunk rejects a nonce length different from the cipher's NonceSize before AEAD.Open.
This later main snapshot still calls AEAD.Open without that guard. It supports this specific hunk-coverage distinction; source alone is not a live service or security qualification.
